articles.headline: JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears
articles.description: JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.
articles.body:
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.

The 16-year-old asked to leave United in September and sources told ESPN that he is on the brink of a move to Real Madrid. He had been training in Madrid earlier this month.

"Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams," he said in the video on Instagram.

"Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I'll always treasure.

"To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ."

- Man United's JJ Gabriel amid Real Madrid move talk: 'Dream to win a Ballon d'Or'

- Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at height of Man United career

United will consider legal action if they believe illegal approaches were made while Gabriel was under contract at Old Trafford, sources said.

Gabriel's Irish passport, which allows him to join any club in the European Union, could help facilitate the transfer under FIFA regulations governing international moves for players aged between 16 and 18, with January the first opportunity for him to be registered.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Fantasy football flex and superflex rankings for Week 11
articles.description: Trying to decide between a couple of closely ranked players this week? Eric Karabell's ranks are here to help.
articles.body:

Still, we must carry on, and this week we have a new overall flex leader, but not a terribly surprising name. The Cincinnati Bengals are piling on the offensive numbers recently, and QB Joe Burrow and WR Ja'Marr Chase are ranked notably well here.

Matchups always matter, too, which is why this season's top RB (Jahmyr Gibbs) is not the top RB (Kenneth Walker III) for this week, and quarterbacks occupy most of the top spots. As always, see which offense gets to face the dreadful Dallas Cowboys, and act accordingly. The San Francisco 49ers go from facing the Cowboys to the difficult Minnesota Vikings, but we don't recommend sitting your top 49ers.

If your league is a standard flex, note that rankings without QBs appear below the superflex rankings. However you prefer to play, good luck this week!

These ranks have been refreshed to take out players from Thursday's Colts-Texans game.

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball adds and NBA bets: Ride with Doncic and Grimes on Tuesday
articles.description: Eric Moody breaks down Tuesday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
articles.body:
Luka Doncic has scored at least 40 points in seven of 12 games this season, including a 43-point performance against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. The Los Angeles Lakers (12-2) have won eight straight and will again be without Austin Reaves when they host the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday's five-game slate.

Cade Cunningham and the Detroit Pistons (8-4) visit the San Antonio Spurs (12-2), who have won 12 straight behind Victor Wembanyama. The big man has averaged 28.6 PPG, 11.6 RPG and 4.3 BPG.

The Minnesota Timberwolves (10-4) host the Portland Trail Blazers for the second consecutive night after Terrence Shannon Jr. scored a career-high 34 points in Monday's win. Shannon has helped pick up the slack with Anthony Edwards sidelined.

Karl-Anthony Towns leads the league with 13.9 RPG and faces the Toronto Raptors again Tuesday after grabbing 17 rebounds against them Sunday.

The Los Angeles Clippers host a Utah Jazz team that has lost 10 straight and will be without Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

Let's take a closer look at Tuesday's matchups, along with some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

Kris Dunn, PG/SG, Los Angeles Clippers (rostered in 30.5% of ESPN leagues)

Dunn has averaged 7.8 PPG, 3.8 RPG, 4.2 APG and 2.0 SPG this season, but managers should be aware that he's played 20 or fewer minutes in three consecutive games. That limits his appeal in points leagues. However, Tuesday's matchup against a Jazz team that commits turnovers on 14.3% of its possessions presents an opportunity for Dunn to contribute defensively. The Clippers also play Thursday and Saturday. If you're expecting a competitive matchup in the steals category this week, Dunn is someone I'd target despite his recent decline in minutes.

Quentin Grimes, SG/SF, Los Angeles Lakers (29.8%)

Grimes has averaged 19.0 PPG, 3.3 RPG, 3.3 APG and 2.3 SPG in 35.7 minutes across his three starts this season. Reaves, who's averaged 38.6 fantasy points per game this season, has already been ruled out against the Hornets on Tuesday. Grimes finished 40 fantasy points in 37 minutes against the Suns on Sunday. Playing alongside Doncic should continue to generate quality perimeter looks for him. You can comfortably roster Grimes in both points and category leagues until Reaves returns, especially since the Lakers face a short-handed Jazz team Wednesday.

Derrick Jones Jr., SF/PF, Los Angeles Clippers (14.6%)

Jones has been one of the more productive category league options available on the wire. He's averaged 11.6 PPG, 4.8 RPG, 2.2 triples and 2.6 combined steals and blocks over his last five games. Jones has played at least 24 minutes in every game this season. Tuesday's matchup against a Jazz defense allowing 118.0 PPG is favorable, especially with Brandon Ingram and Bradley Beal sidelined. articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: AC Milan, Juventus eye USMNT's Folarin Balogun
articles.description: AS Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun is reportedly linked to two of Italy's biggest clubs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw is on the radar of Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus ahead of the January transfer window, Calciomercato has reported. The USMNT striker's agent Jorge Mendes has contacted both clubs, who are looking to strengthen their attacking options, after a €40 million move to Everton collapsed at the end of the last window. The 25-year-old, who is under contract at Monaco until June 2028, is reportedly open to the idea of playing in Serie A.

- Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies' backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.

- Real Madrid are weighing up a move to bring Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Chema Andrés back to the club, as per TEAMtalk. Chema, 21, came through the Madrid youth team ranks but left in 2025 and has impressed since arriving at VfB Stuttgart in the summer. However, a deal could be complicated as there is uncertainty over his contractual situation, with Brighton previously disputing suggestions that Madrid retain an option to re-sign him permanently. Madrid also monitoring highly-rated Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for £46 million this summer.

- Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City's financial charges.

- Bayern Munich youth goalkeeper Leonard Prescott could leave  on a free transfer next summer, after contract talks stalled, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Brighton and Aston Villa are among the clubs tracking his development, says Sky Germany. Prescott, 17, was born in New York but has represented Germany at U17 and is very highly rated.

articles.headline: Irving, Walker III, Bowers and more Knockout league pickups for Week 11
articles.description: As the number of teams shrink, the number of stars available in Knockout leagues grows. Here are the ones to get.
articles.body:
Lady Luck's influence on Knockout leagues is growing ever greater.

Bad fortune in the injury department spawned the largest knockout rate by any individual player all season in Week 10. Drake Maye's likely season-ending fractured ankle not only set back his New England Patriots' playoff chances, but also eliminated his Knockout teams in 21.7% of leagues.

Brock Bowers' own ankle injury landed him high on the list, as he played only 19% of the Las Vegas Raiders' snaps, scored a season-low 3.8 fantasy points and was on knocked-out teams in 13.1% of leagues. Fellow tight end Travis Kelce, who battled ankle and calf issues in what was a 5.0-fantasy-point Week 10, was on knocked-out teams in 12.0% of leagues. Meanwhile, Kenneth Walker III and Puka Nacua, both ruled out in advance of their games, had 16.3% and 12.8% knockout rates.

But it's not only injuries that prove problematic at this midseason stage of Knockout leagues. Unfortunate outcomes, especially those in what were favorable matchups on paper, prove comparably devastating. Chris Olave scored 6.0 fantasy points and had a 13.1% knockout rate, while his WR1 counterpart from that same game, Tetairoa McMillan, scored 6.5 points and was knocked out in 12.2% of leagues. Jonathan Taylor scored 12.3 points and had a 12.2% knockout rate.

It's fantasy football, and anything can happen. But that doesn't mean we should adopt a throw-up-our-hands, aw-shucks type of approach. Rather, the increasingly devastating effects of such unexpected bad outcomes reminds us of two critical Knockout strategies as we progress through the season's second half:

Upside becomes increasingly important each successive week, in order to give us the high-level scores to neutralize these untimely stinkers, and

Bad matchups are a no today, and they're a no tomorrow, a NO the next week, and so on.

As Week 11 dawns, it's that latter point that rings loudest.

We saw the impact of that must-avoid Minnesota Vikings matchup in Week 10, as once-red-hot Green Bay Packers players Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden all finished with 12 or fewer fantasy points, and each of them resided on knocked-out teams in at least 11% of leagues. That comes on the heels of Josh Allen scoring a season-low 12.86 fantasy points against those same Vikings in Week 9, leading to his teams' elimination in 13.1% of leagues.

This week, we've got several significant fantasy football superstars facing the two all-around toughest matchups: The Detroit Lions and San Francisco 49ers, both of whom rank among the top five offenses in terms of points and yards per game, draw the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Vikings.

This isn't to say that Jahmyr Gibbs, Christian McCaffrey and Amon-Ra St. Brown are all instant sits due to the relative downside of their matchups. articles.description: With the season's first month nearly in the books, Ben Golliver examines the biggest storyline so far for all 30 teams.

articles.descriptionJa: シーズンの最初の1ヶ月がほぼ終了した今、ベン・ゴリバーが全30チームについて、これまでの最大の注目ポイントを検証します。
articles.body:
The NBA season is a month old, which makes this a natural time to take stock of all 30 teams.

The San Antonio Spurs, Los Angeles Lakers, Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics sit atop the standings, the defending champion New York Knicks are treading water and several aspiring contenders are juggling star injuries.

And even though Thanksgiving is still more than a week away, the Oklahoma City Thunder have already executed a rare early-season trade and the New Orleans Pelicans have already fielded a public trade request.

With so many developments to wade through, here's what we've learned about all 30 teams since opening night.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

The first month revealed ... Kingston Flemings is a great fit

To no great surprise, Hawks coach Quin Snyder opened the season with a starting lineup -- Nickeil Alexander-Walker, CJ McCollum, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu -- that boasted a phenomenal plus-20.3 net rating in 391 minutes in 2025-26. That decision, which favored experience and continuity, left 2026 lottery pick Flemings and offseason trade acquisitions Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins as reserves.

But Atlanta's starters weren't nearly as potent on offense in the early going as they were last season, so Snyder rejiggered his lineup by replacing the 35-year-old McCollum with the 19-year-old Flemings after only eight games. Atlanta's starters have played at a faster pace and boasted a stingier defense since the move, albeit in a small sample size.

Though Flemings is unlikely to generate Rookie of the Year buzz with several of his draft classmates posting huge numbers, he should be in the All-Rookie mix because he already has distinguished himself in a veteran-dominated rotation with serious playoff aspirations.

The No. 8 pick fits Atlanta's blueprint perfectly: He's confident on the ball but doesn't overly dominate possessions, he can space the court with a dependable outside shot, and he's a pesky defender who thrives in an up-tempo style.

Boston Celtics

The first month revealed ... There is life after Jaylen Brown

Boston's blockbuster summer trade of Brown to Philadelphia for Paul George was met with shock, sadness and anger in some corners of the Celtics' fanbase. Brown stoked those hard feelings last month by playing up the tension with former teammate Jayson Tatum: "There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy."

Unfortunately for Brown, he played like Hamburger Helper in his first game against his former team last week, a blowout victory for the Celtics. Though that high-profile showdown wasn't representative of Philadelphia's strong start, it was further proof that Boston has moved on smoothly after the breakup. As of Tuesday, the Celtics boast the East's best offensive rating and point differential.

articles.headline: Is Chuba Hubbard the biggest X factor to spark a Panthers turnaround?
articles.description: Meet Carolina's team captain, a locker room leader and a relentless running back who is "chasing greatness myself."
articles.body:
Editor's note: Panthers RB Chuba Hubbard finished Sunday's 20-17 win at New Orleans with 92 rushing yards, two rushing touchdowns and 80 receiving yards. This story originally published Friday, Nov. 13 as a preview to Carolina's Week 10 matchup.

CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Chuba Hubbard knows that no one is perfect. But that hasn't stopped the Carolina Panthers' running back from chasing perfection. And after a forgettable, injury-marred 2025 campaign, during which he lost his starting job after a career season in 2024, the team captain is leading the backfield again, and he's perhaps better than ever.

"I pride myself in hard work and staying consistent in knowing what I can do and trying to bring my best every single day, so it's more so just fighting for excellence and fighting to be perfect in every way possible," Hubbard told ESPN.

Hubbard, 27, signed a four-year, $33.2 million contract extension during his breakout 2024 campaign, when he rushed for 1,195 yards and produced 11 total touchdowns in 15 games. Through eight games in 2026, he has rushed for 619 yards and produced seven total touchdowns, bouncing back as the Panthers have struggled to find consistency almost everywhere else during a three-game losing streak and a 3-5 start.

But those numbers don't tell the complete story of Hubbard's value. He's talented, sure, but his true worth is as a tone-setter for the organization.

Though he was selected by the franchise, while Matt Rhule was the coach, in the fourth round of the 2021 NFL draft, Hubbard has established himself as the standard-bearer for the Dave Canales era over the past three seasons. And with Carolina fighting to maintain its position atop the NFC South, his value has become apparent, if not paramount, to the team's ability to recalibrate its season.

"What I love about Chuba is that the things that we talk about wanting to be as an organization, he represents those in spades," Canales said. "His preparation, the way that he works, the way I have to kind of reel him in and call him back a little bit because he goes so hard."

Hubbard could be the X factor who wills Carolina to a win Sunday at the Caesars Superdome (1 p.m. ET, Fox), where the Panthers haven't won since the 2022 season. Hubbard, who has 70.8% of the team's carries this season, will face the New Orleans Saints, who have one of the league's worst rushing defenses (ranked 29th). A win could reignite Carolina's hopes of securing consecutive division titles for the first time since the franchise owned the NFC South crown from 2013 to 2015.

According to those who know him best, Hubbard is ready to shoulder that burden, not only because of who he is as a player, but also because of who he is as a person and a leader in the locker room.

Chuba Hubbard's style 'keeps a defense honest' and could bode well in New Orleans

articles.headline: Expected fantasy points (xFP): 2026 leaderboard for TEs
articles.description: xFP focuses solely on opportunity. Here are the leaders for 2026.
articles.body:
Expected fantasy points (xFP) strips away player talent and efficiency and focuses solely on opportunity.

FORP -- fantasy points over replacement player -- is the difference between a player's actual fantasy point total (FF points) and his xFP (or expected total).

Tight end adjustments are made as follows:

Rushing attempts: No change

Rushing yardage: Rush attempts multiplied by a rusher's expected yardage based on position and rush direction

Rushing touchdowns: Rushing xTD

Targets: No change

Receptions: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected catch rate based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving yardage: Targets multiplied by a receiver's expected yardage based on depth of throw, location and position

Receiving touchdowns: Receiving xTD

Two-point conversions: xTD multiplied by the league average 2-point rate

Fumbles lost: Touches multiplied by the league average rate

Return touchdowns: Excluded due to extreme rareness and randomness

articles.headline: Fantasy notebook: Karabell on Walker Kessler, Joel Embiid, Davion Mitchell, more
articles.description: Eric Karabell empties out the notebook with all that he's noticing around the NBA and what it means for fantasy.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers PG Luka Doncic is enjoying a remarkable start to the season, averaging 39.0 PPG and 65.8 ESPN fantasy points per game. Meanwhile, SG/PG Austin Reaves is delivering big numbers as well, with 24.7 PPG and terrific shooting. He ranks among the top 15 players on ESPN's Player Rater, and he is top 30 in points formats. Then again, these were not necessarily draft-day bargains. Investors expected monster numbers.

Lakers C Walker Kessler, however, was barely among the top 50 selections in ESPN average live drafts. It seemed optimistic at the time, since Kessler participated in a mere five games last season for the Utah Jazz before a torn labrum in his left shoulder ended his season. Kessler was off to a solid start in that small sample, averaging 14.4 PPG, 10.8 RPG and 1.8 BPG, while hitting 70.3% of his field goals. Wow, wouldn't it be nice if he could do that for 70-plus games? The Lakers hoped so when they acquired him through a July trade.

Kessler enters Tuesday's game with the Charlotte Hornets averaging 14.5 PPG, 10.9 RPG and 2.2 BPG, while hitting 68% of his field goals (which leads the NBA). Hmm, those numbers look awfully similar to last season's five-game sample, and they are tremendously valuable. Kessler is seventh on the Player Rater (roto/categories leagues) and 10th in points formats, averaging 41.4 fantasy points per game, a true fantasy MVP candidate. Tuesday's home game against Charlotte will be Kessler's first missed game, which is also significant.

Fantasy managers love all this, of course, but they also must be wondering how long these numbers can last. After all, Kessler, 25, has never delivered numbers like this for a sustained period of time. Should fantasy managers trade him? Kessler boasts more fantasy points than stars Jayson Tatum, Karl-Anthony Towns, Kevin Durant and Donovan Mitchell. A wise fantasy manager would trade Kessler for any of those fellows, of course. What about top 20 picks Amen Thompson, LaMelo Ball and Trae Young?

Much of this is dependent on your league(s) format. In points formats, where statistical versatility is not so relevant (everyone can just score and rebound and never block a shot, for example), it is smart to sell high on players off to great starts that may be overachieving and may not be so durable. In roto formats, however, players that excel in harder-to-get categories such as blocked shots, steals (Dyson Daniels, for example) and perhaps field goal shooting carry unique value.

Nobody wants to punt blocked shots in a roto league if they don't need to, but some may be forced to. Keep Kessler around in a roto format (and hope for 70-plus games), but in a points format, it may be time to perhaps seek a trade partner, just in case.

articles.headline: The clock is ticking on Steph Curry's final act with the Warriors
articles.description: At 38, Curry is still brilliant -- but managing his body has become the biggest battle of his career.
articles.headlineJa: ステフィン・カリー、ウォリアーズでの「ラストダンス」へのカウントダウン
articles.descriptionJa: 38歳となったカリーは依然として輝きを放っているが、身体のコンディション管理がキャリア最大の戦いとなっている。
articles.body:
LATE LAST JANUARY, during an off-day workout in an empty downtown Minneapolis arena, Stephen Curry's right knee started bothering him.

Four days prior, he had been named an All-Star starter for an 11th time, averaging 27.2 points on extreme efficiency, keeping the Golden State Warriors' record at a respectable 25-21.

But his co-star, Jimmy Butler, had torn his right ACL the week before. Curry, at 37, was again dealing with overloaded schemes and an increased offensive burden. His knee started barking.

"That was the moment where I started to get concerned," Curry said. "It just didn't feel right."

Curry attempted to play through what he described as "a weird soreness and pain that didn't go away." Despite being initially listed as questionable, he had 26 points against the Timberwolves, rested for a game and then scored 27 in Utah to close the road trip and 23 against the Detroit Pistons once the team returned home.

But neither the pain nor concern would subside.

"Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, 'Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'" Curry said. "And I was just faking it for the first whatever [25 minutes]."

There's something poetic about his final sequence before he left the game. Curry came off a third-quarter pindown into an isolation against Ausar Thompson and did what he described as "a high-step thing because it hurt so bad in that moment."

After the fidget, Curry shook Thompson with a crossover combination, hobbled into the lane and poured in an and-1 floater over one of the best perimeter defenders in the world to give him 23 points in those 25 minutes.

But then he limped to the sideline and told Rick Celebrini -- the franchise's lead medical decision-maker whom Curry trusts implicitly -- that the swelling and stiffness had become too much to bear.

"I got smart about the situation," said Curry, who missed the next 27 games. "We had to go get scans."

This is the dichotomy of the still-spectacular Curry in the twilight stage of his Hall of Fame career. On the court, he can still string together what coach Steve Kerr calls "magical" performances.

But away from the fireworks show, Curry is in a constant race against time, obsessively evolving his body-maintenance plan in an effort to be available as often as possible -- until the clock runs out.

Ten days ago, Curry sat down with ESPN to discuss the physical and mental challenges of the moment, mostly centered on the management of a knee injury that derailed his 17th season -- and led to the Warriors tumbling to 37-45 and missing the playoffs.

One night after the conversation, he scorched the Orlando Magic for 41 points, surpassing LeBron James and Michael Jordan for the most 40-point games after age 35 in NBA history, continuing a surge that spiked the Warriors' record to 8-3 and indicated his offensive game was as sharp as ever.

articles.descriptionJa: 夏の移籍を巡る不透明な状況とシーズン序盤の不調を経て、ヴィニシウス・ジュニオールはレアル・マドリードとブラジル代表で復活への道を歩んでいる。
articles.body:
Vinícius Júnior has earned hundreds of millions of euros thanks to his feet. Thunderous goals off his instep, intuitive, imaginative crosses bending in from his outstep, defender-fooling step-overs while full-tilt sprinting at 35kmh. The Real Madrid and Brazil star is a winger who's often been a few steps ahead of opponents.

But the metaphorical "first step" that the 26-year-old took in Singapore on Monday -- starting to solve a problem by admitting that there has been one -- might be the best foot forward he's taken in many months.

You've probably consumed his words by now -- with the same hunger as he appears to have consumed summer treats that the regular Joe is allowed but are next to prohibited for elite athletes. Most especially if, simultaneously, they are skimping on the high-intensity, calorie-burning exercise which is now the regimented, obligatory companion of any top footballer during the brief summer weeks when they're not training and playing.

"I don't think I prepared myself well enough for the new season," Vinícius said. "I took advantage of the holidays to rest, to disconnect from soccer and to spend more family time. The final result was that I trained less than in previous summers."

- Meet Como's Nico Paz, the heir to Lionel Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- As Nike replaces Adidas, is Champions League star ball on its way out?

- 10 Best: Ranking the world's top men's soccer players ... again!

Maybe Vinícius received a timely call from Eden Hazard, the last star to arrive back for a Real Madrid preseason carrying much more weight than is permissible? I'm being fanciful, but wouldn't it be nice to think that one ex-magician might be looking out for a current wing-wizard? Because the Belgian, who still lives in Madrid and remains under the romantic spell of the greatest club in the world (I know because he told me so), is a good morality tale for his Brazilian successor.

"I wouldn't say I was overdoing what I ate -- I just wasn't paying attention," Hazard admitted to L'Equipe soon after he retired from football in 2023, relinquishing a full year of a multi-million contract with Madrid. "I didn't attach any importance to it. I'm a bon vivant; I enjoy eating with friends, having a drink. Dieting sucks -- it's useless ... well, I suppose it's fine if you want to keep playing until you're 40.

"That summer when I arrived at Madrid, I had just finished an incredible season with Chelsea. I told myself, 'Now that I'm at Real, this might be one of the last vacations where I can ... so, I just let myself go."

It cost Hazard acceleration, sharpness of those quick feet of his, injury avoidance, injury recuperation, the faith of his coach, the fans and the media. Reading those words, do you recognise the comparisons with much of Vinícius' season thus far?

Now, Vinícius is a universe away from what became Hazard's extreme situation. But the Brazilian is currently in direct competition for his place on Madrid's left wing with €125 mil
